# AI Security Hub plugin marketplace

One source catalog builds three installable packages: native VS Code Agent Plugins 1.0, company-style Copilot, and Claude Code. The build also generates separate Copilot and Claude marketplaces.

Every package contains all 44 security modules, the Secure Code Review agent, three review commands, two skills, and a session-start reminder. The internal review method remains manually invoked. The new `secure-development` skill routes coding tasks to the baseline and matching security references.

## Compatibility

| Client | Guidance | Review tools |
|---|---|---|
| Current VS Code, Local Copilot sessions | Native `applyTo` rules, preventive skill, session reminder | Native VS Code tools or read/search aliases in the marketplace package |
| Current Copilot CLI | Packaged rules where supported, preventive skill, session reminder | Read/search aliases |
| Current Claude Code | Preventive skill and session reminder | `Read`, `Grep`, `Glob` |

Claude skill selection does not guarantee VS Code's automatic file matching. All security content is included, and the skill instructs the model to consult the matching references. Instructions remain model guidance; retain independent security checks.

The review agents have no shell or editing tools. If the client cannot expose a diff through read-only tools, attach the diff or name files to review. Claude review commands use `context: fork` and the named review agent.

Consumers need no npm install or build step. Hooks print fixed JSON, ignore input, and do not inspect or modify the project or access the network. Copilot uses the host shell on Linux/macOS and Windows PowerShell on Windows; Claude uses its shell environment, including Git Bash on Windows. In VS Code, enable `chat.plugins.enabled` and `chat.useHooks` in a trusted workspace. Enterprise policy can control availability.

## VS Code installation

After committing and pushing these files, add this repository in user settings:

```json
{
  "chat.plugins.enabled": true,
  "chat.useHooks": true,
  "chat.plugins.marketplaces": ["auseraet/ai_security_hub"]
}
```

Search `@agentPlugins` in Extensions and install **ai-security-hub** from **ai-security-hub-marketplace**. Alternatively, run **Chat: Install Plugin From Source** with `https://github.com/auseraet/ai_security_hub`.

For local testing before publication:

```json
{
  "chat.plugins.enabled": true,
  "chat.useHooks": true,
  "chat.pluginLocations": {
    "/absolute/path/to/ai_security_hub/plugins/ai-security-hub": true
  }
}
```

To load the native Agent Plugins 1.0 variant, register the repository root instead. Enable only one variant per workspace. Windows paths can use forward slashes. With WSL, SSH, or containers, use a path visible to the environment loading the plugin.

## Copilot CLI installation

After publishing:

```bash
copilot plugin marketplace add https://github.com/auseraet/ai_security_hub.git
copilot plugin install ai-security-hub@ai-security-hub-marketplace
```

Use `/plugin marketplace add` and `/plugin install` inside an existing session. For local development, add the checkout's absolute path as the marketplace source.

## Claude Code installation

Add the checkout now, or its Git URL after publication:

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add /absolute/path/to/ai_security_hub
claude plugin install ai-security-hub@ai-security-hub-claude
```

To test without installation:

```bash
claude --plugin-dir /absolute/path/to/ai_security_hub/claude-plugins/ai-security-hub
```

Use `/ai-security-hub:secure-code-review`, `/ai-security-hub:review-security-changes`, or `/ai-security-hub:validate-security-finding`. The internal review-method skill is hidden from the command menu.

## Build and release

Maintainers need Node.js 22+, npm, Git, and `tar`. The YAML parser is a pinned build dependency and is not shipped with plugins. Run from the repository root in Bash or PowerShell:

```text
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npm run build
npm run validate
npm test
npm run package
```

Bump **plugin.json's version**, add its entry to `CHANGELOG.md`, rebuild, and commit sources and generated output. The build synchronizes all plugin manifests and both marketplaces. The catalog retains its independent security-content version; `package.json` describes private build tooling.

After committing, check the release against its base:

```text
npm run plugin:check-versions -- --base origin/main
```

The gate rejects shipped changes without an increasing version, missing changelog entries, and generated drift. GitHub Actions and GitLab CI run validation and tests; PR/MR jobs check the actual base. GitLab also rebuilds and rejects uncommitted generated output.

Optional pre-commit automation is configured in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`. After installing `pre-commit`, run `pre-commit install`. The hook rebuilds and stages generated assets only, refuses unstaged shipped-source changes, and never bumps versions. It is not installed automatically.

The existing Bash/PowerShell catalog validators and repository installer tests remain required for changes to those sources.

## Archives and updates

`npm run package` writes these archives with SHA-256 checksums to `dist/`:

| Suffix | Contents |
|---|---|
| `-native-<version>.tar.gz` | Native VS Code package |
| `-copilot-<version>.tar.gz` | Company-style Copilot package |
| `-claude-<version>.tar.gz` | Claude package |
| `-marketplace-<version>.tar.gz` | Both marketplaces, both client packages, and reusable agent/skill sources for central integration |

Extract a package and register the directory containing its manifest. An extracted marketplace archive can be added as a local marketplace. Archives exclude Git history, workspace-only `.github` instructions, dependency installations, and maintainer tooling.

For pinned installations, use a reviewed archive or Git tag and update that directory deliberately. Git/marketplace installations use the client's update command. In current VS Code, run **Extensions: Check for Extension Updates**.

## Authoritative sources and generated output

| Edit here | Generated output |
|---|---|
| `catalog/` | Native rules and skill references |
| `review-pack/.github/` | Agents, commands, internal method |
| `plugin/skills/` | Preventive skill |
| `plugin/hooks/reminder.json` | Platform-specific reminder scripts/configuration |
| `plugin.json` | Versioned client manifests and marketplaces |
| `docs/PLUGIN.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` | Package documentation |

`agents/`, `skills/`, `com.github.copilot/`, `plugins/`, and `claude-plugins/` are generated. Claude output stays outside `plugins/` to prevent duplicate discovery. The Copilot package has a root manifest for current client discovery and the company-required `.github/plugin/plugin.json` sidecar.

The runtime loads `commands/` and `hooks/hooks.json`. Equivalent `prompts/` files and `hooks/copilot-agents-source.json` support the reference company's translator; they are not additional runtime registrations.

## Company marketplace integration

Merge the marketplace archive's `agents/`, `skills/`, and `plugins/ai-security-hub/` into the corresponding central directories, resolving name collisions. Run that repository's build and validation workflow to regenerate its marketplaces. Do not overwrite the central catalogs with this single-plugin catalog.

The Hub checkout retains its own repository-local `.github` review pack for installer checks. That duplicate local skill is excluded from the integration export; copying the whole checkout into the central source tree would fail its duplicate-name validator.

Test the export with a supplied reference checkout without modifying it:

```text
node scripts/check-reference.mjs /path/to/copilot-agents
```

This runs its actual Copilot, skill, and Claude validators in a temporary export. The primary generator preserves explicit client-specific command execution and native rules. The company's translator can produce different metadata, so verify representative workflows after a central rebuild.

## Verify activation

1. Confirm the plugin, review agent, and three commands appear.
2. Start a new session and check hook diagnostics for the reminder.
3. Request a small JavaScript change and a Terraform change; confirm the corresponding security references are used.
4. Review a supplied diff and confirm the agent reports in chat without edits or command execution.

Automated tests cover packaging, relative links, tool restrictions, arguments, hook output, release gates, and archive extraction. They do not replace a model-session check in each installed client.

If an application already has the Hub's generated `.github` instructions and review pack, disable the plugin there until migration to avoid duplicates. The Bash/PowerShell installers remain available for repository-based Copilot surfaces, including GitHub.com workflows.
